title: GPU replenishment velocity and risk dashboard
content:
Purpose:
A real-time human-readable sheet to track incoming GPU shipments, vendor velocity, regional prioritization, and risk adjustments that inform provisioning and live reorder points. This is intended as a working dashboard for the infra procurement rotation; not final artifacts.

Summary snapshot (as of 2026-02-15):
- Total on-hand GPUs across regions: 11,420
- Committed incoming (ordered, shipping/not received): 7,350
- Available usable capacity after calibration/reserves: ~9,900 (post-quantization plan)
- Shortfall vs projected throughput demand (next 180 days): 2,100 GPUs (mid-case)

Key table: incoming pipeline (condensed)
Columns: shipment_id | sku | qty | vendor | origin | est-lead-days | lead-stddev | eta-window | region-priority | risk-level | mitigation
- S-2026-011 | H100-80GB | 1,200 | VendorA | Taiwan | 45 | 10 | 2026-03-02 - 2026-03-18 | us-west, eu-central | medium | secure rail uplift, hold 100 units for canary
- S-2026-009 | A100-40GB | 600 | VendorB | Korea | 72 | 25 | 2026-04-10 - 2026-05-05 | us-east | high | re-route to fast air (cost +$0.9k/unit)
- S-2026-014 | L40s | 2,000 | VendorC | China (partner) | 30 | 7 | 2026-02-20 - 2026-03-05 | ap-east, eu-west | low | retain for ap-east surge
- S-2026-017 | H200-100GB | 900 | VendorA | Taiwan | 60 | 15 | 2026-03-18 - 2026-04-18 | dedicated-pool | medium-high | split across 2 shipments, partial invoicing
- S-2026-020 | H100-80GB (refurb) | 650 | Secondary | USA | 14 | 6 | 2026-02-22 - 2026-03-02 | internal-test | low | quarantine + qualification tests

Assumptions and notes:
- Lead times track vendor SLA + customs buffer; stddev is empirical from last 9 shipments.
- Regions prioritized using a friction score: (SLA-need * customer-revenue-weight) + (current-utilization/threshold).
- Buffer policy: maintain min buffer = max(0.12 * active-fleet, 30 units per region).
- Refurb counts are counted at 0.8 effective capacity until calibration verified.

Reorder triggers (working rules):
- Auto-raise PO when projected usable-days-to-empty in any region <= 75 days AND forecasted demand growth > 10% over baseline.
- Manual override for enterprise accounts: engineering lead + solutions sign-off for expedited lanes.
- Soft-priority lane for Dedicated pools: maintain 20% of fleet committed as reserved (non-ephemeral).

Vendor velocity and risk profiles (short):
- VendorA (Tier1): steady volume, 3–10% delay probability, good customs paperwork. Preferred for H100/H200 series.
- VendorB (Tier2): lower unit cost, higher lead variance (20–30% delays during Q1 shipments). Avoid sole-source for >800 units.
- VendorC (Channel partner): rapid for L40/Higher volume but regional constraints (limited EU interpos). Use for APAC heavy lifts.
- Secondary/refurb vendors: fast local availability, higher failure/qualification rate (5–12%). Use for test/dev & canaries.

Risk scoring rubric (applied per shipment):
- Low: <10% delay probability, lead-stddev <10 days
- Medium: 10–25% delay, lead-stddev 10–20 days
- High: >25% delay, lead-stddev >20 days or geopolitical routing risk

Region prioritization snapshot:
- us-west: utilization 87% (peak models), buffer 300 units, near-term reorder suggested for H100 capacity
- us-east: utilization 74%, buffer 180 units, short on A100-class for legacy customers
- eu-central: utilization 79%, buffer 140 units, invoice hold causing 2 shipments delay (VendorA)
- ap-east: utilization 65%, buffer 120 units, recommended to accept larger L40 tranche for scale-out tests

Scenario planning (3 lanes):
1) Conservative: 20% slower vendor tempo (lead times +20%), prioritize Dedicated commits, shift 500 units from hosted to dedicated -> shortfall 2,800 GPUs -> action: initiate fast-air for top 1 shipments, renegotiate payment terms.
2) Mid-case (base): current pipeline as listed -> shortfall 2,100 GPUs -> action: pull 650 refurb for dev, squeeze autoscaling tuning to reduce unit need by 6%.
3) Optimistic: vendors speed up (lead times -15%) and L40 uptake increases effective capacity -> shortfall eliminated by Q3 -> action: normal pacing, convert 400 units to reserved for enterprise.

Open decisions / blockers:
- Do we allow VendorB to be sole source for the A100 tranche (S-2026-009)? recommended no; prefer split across VendorA + VendorB.
- Customs broker change: a new broker option can reduce ETA by ~7 days for Taiwan shipments but increases fees. Vote required by procurement by 2026-02-22.
- Quantization/packing changes: if we increase quant tolerance, usable capacity could rise by ~6% — product team feasibility sign-off pending.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Asha: escalate S-2026-009 to vendor and request split shipping plan (due 2026-02-17).
- Diego: run a 30-day utilization simulation applying 6% quant improvement and deliver delta by 2026-02-20.
- Rina: open customs-broker RFP and score 3 brokers (due 2026-02-24).
- Ethan: validate refurb qualification batch S-2026-020 (tests complete by 2026-02-28).

Quick math/operational counters (for sprint sync):
- Incoming units shipping within 30 days: 3,350
- Units with >45-day ETA: 4,900
- Units tagged high-risk: 2,150

Notes for the next review:
- Refresh vendor lead-stddev monthly, include shipment-level tracking numbers and carrier ETAs where available.
- Consider adding a small capital reserve to buy opportunistic mid-quarter vendor surplus.
- If geopolitical constraints escalate, we need pre-approved alternate lanes (list of carriers + customs contacts).

Owner note: this sheet is intentionally concise to support rotation hand-offs. Use the incoming shipment IDs for deeper lookups (linked artifacts). Expect churn; edit freely and surface major deviations in the weekly Infra procurement sync.
